main_text.l: QVI SIBI NIMIVM SAPERE videtur, nequicquam sapit.
[Woodcut illustration: a man in a fur-trimmed robe and hat holding a globe aloft, with a skeleton at right holding an hourglass, a fox at his feet, a cart and a walled town in the background.]
Est leuis ac vanus qui plus sibi vendicat ipse,
Ne nimium sapias, pudor est mage velle videri:
Qui sapit hoc vere quod sapit, ille sapit.
